title: Just get on with it!
paragraphs: Do you ever have a task that needs doing, but however urgent it is, you just don't get down to it? From doing the housework to writing an assignment, there's always something I can put off until tomorrow.

Being a procrastinator is quite easy. There are so many other more interesting distractions such as watching funny cat videos on the internet or catching up with friends on social media! But Benjamin Franklin, one of the Founding Fathers of the United States, once wisely said that: 'You may delay, but time will not', in other words, the time we waste now is gone forever - so maybe I should pull my socks up and get on with what I should be doing.

The reason why many of us delay doing something is that we live for the present not the future. We are reluctant to engage in tasks that relate to the future - sorting something out now that will benefit us in the future doesn't seem a priority. Daphna Oyserman, Professor of Psychology at the University of Southern California, says: "Many of the future things that are very important require that we start now rather than later... Later means we don't have a lot of time left." So get cracking now rather than have a last-minute panic!

But it's hard to muster any enthusiasm when there are tedious chores to be done, so how can I control my lack of focus and knuckle down to what really needs to be done? One idea is temptation bundling - doing two activities together - one that is boring but essential and one that you enjoy but isn't so productive. Planning is essential too and we should never underestimate how long things will take us. However, Dr Catherine Loveday from Westminster University warns us about a 'planning fallacy' thinking we can get something done quickly. She says "We never seem to get any better at judging how long things will take us."

vocabulary.entry: urgent [adj.] /ˈɜːdʒənt/ 紧急的；急迫的
vocabulary.example: The patient needs urgent medical attention.
vocabulary.translation: 这位病人需要紧急医疗救治。

vocabulary.entry: get down to [phr.] /ɡet daʊn tuː/ 开始认真做 (固定搭配)
vocabulary.example: It's time to get down to work.
vocabulary.translation: 是时候开始认真工作了。

vocabulary.entry: put off [phr.] /pʊt ɒf/ 推迟；拖延 (固定搭配)
vocabulary.example: Don't put off until tomorrow what you can do today.
vocabulary.translation: 今天能做的事不要拖到明天。

vocabulary.entry: procrastinator [n.] /prəʊˈkræstɪneɪtə/ 拖延者
vocabulary.example: As a procrastinator, he often misses deadlines.
vocabulary.translation: 作为一个拖延者，他经常错过截止日期。

vocabulary.entry: distraction [n.] /dɪˈstrækʃən/ 使人分心的事物
vocabulary.example: Social media is a major distraction for students.
vocabulary.translation: 社交媒体是让学生分心的主要因素。

vocabulary.entry: pull my socks up [phr.] /pʊl maɪ sɒks ʌp/ 振作起来；努力改进 (英式英语；口语；固定搭配)
vocabulary.example: I need to pull my socks up and study harder.
vocabulary.translation: 我需要振作起来，更加努力地学习。

vocabulary.entry: get on with [phr.] /ɡet ɒn wɪð/ 继续做；开始做 (固定搭配)
vocabulary.example: Stop talking and get on with your work.
vocabulary.translation: 别说话了，继续做你的工作。

vocabulary.entry: reluctant [adj.] /rɪˈlʌktənt/ 不情愿的；勉强的 (书面语)
vocabulary.example: She was reluctant to admit her mistake.
vocabulary.translation: 她不情愿承认自己的错误。

vocabulary.entry: engage in [phr.] /ɪnˈɡeɪdʒ ɪn/ 从事；参与 (书面语)
vocabulary.example: He engages in voluntary work at weekends.
vocabulary.translation: 他周末从事志愿工作。

vocabulary.entry: sort out [phr.] /sɔːt aʊt/ 解决；整理 (固定搭配)
vocabulary.example: We need to sort out this problem quickly.
vocabulary.translation: 我们需要尽快解决这个问题。

vocabulary.entry: priority [n.] /praɪˈɒrəti/ 优先事项；首要事情
vocabulary.example: Safety is our top priority.
vocabulary.translation: 安全是我们的首要任务。

vocabulary.entry: get cracking [phr.] /ɡet ˈkrækɪŋ/ 赶紧开始做；加紧干 (英式英语；口语；固定搭配)
vocabulary.example: We need to get cracking if we want to finish on time.
vocabulary.translation: 如果我们想按时完成，就需要赶紧开始。

vocabulary.entry: last-minute panic [n.] /ˌlɑːst ˈmɪnɪt ˈpænɪk/ 最后一刻的惊慌失措 (固定搭配)
vocabulary.example: A last-minute panic is not an effective way to work.
vocabulary.translation: 最后一刻的惊慌失措不是有效的工作方式。

vocabulary.entry: muster [v.] /ˈmʌstə/ 鼓起；聚集 (书面语)
vocabulary.example: He mustered the courage to speak in public.
vocabulary.translation: 他鼓起勇气在公众面前讲话。

vocabulary.entry: tedious [adj.] /ˈtiːdiəs/ 乏味的；单调的
vocabulary.example: Data entry can be a tedious job.
vocabulary.translation: 数据录入可能是一份乏味的工作。

vocabulary.entry: knuckle down [phr.] /ˈnʌkəl daʊn/ 开始认真做；埋头苦干 (口语；固定搭配)
vocabulary.example: You need to knuckle down and finish your thesis.
vocabulary.translation: 你需要开始认真做，完成你的论文。

vocabulary.entry: temptation bundling [n.] /tempˈteɪʃən ˈbʌndlɪŋ/ 诱惑捆绑 (专业词汇；行为心理学)
vocabulary.example: Temptation bundling combines a guilty pleasure with a productive task.
vocabulary.translation: 诱惑捆绑将一个令人内疚的快乐和一个富有成效的任务结合起来。

vocabulary.entry: underestimate [v.] /ˌʌndərˈestɪmeɪt/ 低估
vocabulary.example: Don't underestimate the difficulty of the task.
vocabulary.translation: 不要低估这项任务的难度。

vocabulary.entry: planning fallacy [n.] /ˈplænɪŋ ˈfæləsi/ 计划谬误 (专业词汇；心理学)
vocabulary.example: The planning fallacy leads us to think we can finish faster than we actually can.
vocabulary.translation: 计划谬误让我们认为自己能比实际更快完成。

vocabulary.entry: crack on [phr.] /kræk ɒn/ 继续快速做；加紧干 (英式英语；口语；固定搭配)
vocabulary.example: We'd better crack on with the report.
vocabulary.translation: 我们最好加紧写报告。

vocabulary.entry: productive [adj.] /prəˈdʌktɪv/ 富有成效的
vocabulary.example: She had a productive day at the office.
vocabulary.translation: 她在办公室度过了富有成效的一天。

vocabulary.entry: catch up with [phr.] /kætʃ ʌp wɪð/ 与……叙旧；了解近况 (固定搭配)
vocabulary.example: I need to catch up with my old friends.
vocabulary.translation: 我需要和我的老朋友叙叙旧。

sentences.english: Do you ever have a task that needs doing, but however urgent it is, you just don't get down to it?
sentences.chinese: 你是否曾经有一项需要完成的任务，但是不管它有多紧急，你就是不着手去做呢？

sentences.english: From doing the housework to writing an assignment, there's always something I can put off until tomorrow.
sentences.chinese: 从做家务到写作业，总是有些事情我可以推迟到明天再做。

sentences.english: Being a procrastinator is quite easy.
sentences.chinese: 成为一个拖延者很容易。

sentences.english: There are so many other more interesting distractions such as watching funny cat videos on the internet or catching up with friends on social media!
sentences.chinese: 还有很多其他更有趣的让人分心的事物，比如在互联网上看看有趣的猫咪视频，或者在社交媒体上和朋友们叙旧！

sentences.english: But Benjamin Franklin, one of the Founding Fathers of the United States, once wisely said that: 'You may delay, but time will not', in other words, the time we waste now is gone forever - so maybe I should pull my socks up and get on with what I should be doing.
sentences.chinese: 但是美国开国元勋之一的本杰明·富兰克林曾经明智地说过：“你可以拖延，但时间不会”，换句话说，我们现在浪费的时间一去不复返了——所以也许我应该振作起来，继续去做我应该做的事情。

sentences.english: The reason why many of us delay doing something is that we live for the present not the future.
sentences.chinese: 我们很多人拖延做某事的原因是我们为当下而活，而不是为未来而活。

sentences.english: We are reluctant to engage in tasks that relate to the future - sorting something out now that will benefit us in the future doesn't seem a priority.
sentences.chinese: 我们不愿意去做那些与未来相关的任务——现在解决一些对未来有益的事情似乎不是优先考虑的事情。

sentences.english: Daphna Oyserman, Professor of Psychology at the University of Southern California, says: "Many of the future things that are very important require that we start now rather than later... Later means we don't have a lot of time left."
sentences.chinese: 南加州大学的心理学教授达夫娜·奥伊瑟曼说：“许多与未来非常重要的事情都要求我们现在就开始行动，而不是等到以后......等到以后意味着我们没有太多时间了。”

sentences.english: So get cracking now rather than have a last-minute panic!
sentences.chinese: 所以现在就去做吧，而不是到最后一刻才惊慌失措！

sentences.english: But it's hard to muster any enthusiasm when there are tedious chores to be done, so how can I control my lack of focus and knuckle down to what really needs to be done?
sentences.chinese: 但是，当有乏味的琐事要做时，很难鼓起任何热情，那么我该如何控制自己注意力不集中，并开始认真做真正需要做的事情呢？

sentences.english: One idea is temptation bundling - doing two activities together - one that is boring but essential and one that you enjoy but isn't so productive.
sentences.chinese: 一个想法是诱惑捆绑——将两项活动一起做——一项无聊但必不可少，另一项你喜欢但效率不高。

sentences.english: Planning is essential too and we should never underestimate how long things will take us.
sentences.chinese: 计划也很重要，我们绝不应低估事情会花费我们多长时间。

sentences.english: However, Dr Catherine Loveday from Westminster University warns us about a 'planning fallacy' thinking we can get something done quickly.
sentences.chinese: 然而，威斯敏斯特大学的凯瑟琳·洛夫迪博士警告我们注意“计划谬误”，即认为我们可以快速完成某事。

sentences.english: She says "We never seem to get any better at judging how long things will take us."
sentences.chinese: 她说：“我们在判断事情需要多长时间方面似乎从未有所提高。”
